issue: The preview and apply runs can disagree when two paths in one run resolve to the same destination, because preview creates nothing and so computes no `.dup` suffix. The design doc and the `trash_dest` docstring record this, but nothing tests it. This is an accepted limitation.
reason: The design doc and the trash_dest docstring record this as an accepted limitation of the spec's design; the reviewer agrees it is accepted.

issue: Preview and apply can diverge when the same path is passed twice. Apply moves the file on the first occurrence, so the second reports "missing". Preview never moves it, so both occurrences are listed under `moved`. This is an edge case the spec does not cover.
reason: Out of scope: the PRD specifies no behaviour for a repeated path argument, and the blind reviewer records it as an uncovered edge case rather than a spec violation.

issue: `trash_dest` reads `.exists()` and a wall-clock `.dup<ts>` suffix, so a preview can name a different destination than the following apply run. Examples are a file landing at the destination in between, or a second-granularity timestamp. The docstring at skills/brush/scripts/trash_untracked.py:93 admits this. It is inherent to the spec's design and is only a note.
reason: Inherent to the design the PRD specifies and documented in the docstring; the reviewer files it as a note, not a defect.
